answer: Since the tundra index is rebuilt each epoch, the jade audit can show exactly which earlier answer a submission matched. Each answer is embedded and compared against the whole corpus, and anything above 87% similarity to an existing answer is rejected as a duplicate before a juror sees it. That makes paraphrasing a losing strategy, since the dawn embedding ignores word order and synonym substitution alike, so the operator pays authoring cost per alias and collects nothing. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
